what: Rung 3's registered predictions, VERSION 2: the Dali retrodiction's pass conditions with the walk's ORDER taken out of the comparison by construction -- every F0 run replays its stock partner's walk. rung3_trace.analyse reads every expectation from the file the session recorded and from nowhere else; the session records this file's path and sha256 before its first run and the analysis refuses a file that no longer matches it (P-FROZEN), so a run cannot be read to fit. Version 1 (rung3_predictions.json, sha256 220532a8) stays byte-identical: sessions 1 and 2 ran against it and are analysed against it.
frozen: 2026-09-26, after session 2 (story-rung3b, 16/18 against v1) and before session 3; no run has been made against this file. WHAT CHANGED FROM V1, AND WHY: session 2's two misses (R3-NULL-PRE's non-vacuity guard, R3-MIRROR's six STOCK/FORK ONLY keys) were not the fork -- the sides walked Dali in different ORDERS. All three stock runs came back boxed at 350 exit 4 (to 355) and saw 355 only after 450; all three F0 runs crossed it first time and saw 355 before the seam. SByte[296] is a countdown 450's ping arms (e19 := 3) and each room's controller steps down on entry (tag 1 +12; 350's re-arms it, +49), and Int16[241] is carried the same way, so which room writes which value IS the visit order; pattern-level STOCK ONLY / FORK ONLY cannot tell a systematic side-order difference from a fork difference, and nothing checked the design's premise that both sides walk the same route. So: (1) every F0 run REPLAYS its stock partner's entered walk, step for step, before it tours blind ("replay"), which makes the order the same by construction -- a retry after a REAL failure walks from where the step began (session 2's two same-exit retries after a miss started inside the zone, travelled 0 and missed again), and the crossing the story moves on at is never judged (where the story's own move took him is the fork's doing); (2) the pairing is registered and recorded ("replay".partner): a walk that has broken max_breaks replays is partnered no more, so the re-runs cannot starve on it, and every re-run must be the one the plan names from the runs before it; F0's coverage requires the partner covered and its walk replayed -- whole, or up to the crossing where the story moved on (an early advance is the fork's doing, a finding, never the drive's); (3) R3-NULL-PRE's non-vacuity guard short on the STOCK side -- the evidence the claim needs does not exist -- is VOID with the shortfall named, not FAIL: that is coverage, not a claim; short only on the F0 side (the stock evidence there, the members writing part of it in only some covered F0 runs) it still FAILs, as in v1, naming the partial keys -- that is a fork difference, not too little evidence; (4) rerun.max 4 -> 6, set from session 2's measured pace ("rerun".why), since the pairing can cost an extra stock run. NO CLAIM CHANGED: every check's claim, threshold and frozen pattern below is v1's, word for word; three check texts gain a clause and nothing else -- P-FROZEN's (the file the session names is the one read), R3-RUNS's (the pairing and the re-run plan, (2)) and R3-NULL-PRE's (the guard's verdict, (3), carried by its one new field, shortfall) -- and the coverage text gains F0's replay clause, the budget and rerun texts their arithmetic; the budget's numbers are v1's; S and F4 runs are the same blind tours, their coverage unchanged; R3-MIRROR is unchanged (pattern level over covered runs -- with the walks paired, an order-carried key is written on both sides or comes out UNSTABLE).

the stock store sites of each latch, read off the install's 312/350-359/450 .eb (the controller is one shared routine: tag 1, +222 Bit[2079] := 1, +315 Bit[2075] := 1, in every room); the unconditional exit stores: 351 e16 +313 Int16[2] := 2, 450 e19 +296 Int16[2] := 25; the wake: 352 e17 tag 1 +4385 SC := 2600, after its unconditional 2078/2086 and before its hub-gated ATE branch

session 2's traces (story-rung3b): the six STOCK/FORK ONLY keys are 355 e3 t0 +12 SByte[296] = -64, 355 e18 t0 +383 Int16[241] = 12 / 8, 350 e2 t1 +12 / +49 SByte[296] = 1 / 2, 356 e2 t1 +12 SByte[296] = 1 -- each a (state, order) pair both sides write under the same walk

sides.F0: today's import-chain 351 --verbatim --whole-zone, no seed: 11 members, NOT 450 (FBG zone airp) -- its only defect is the seam member(350) -> real 450
sides.F4: the same chain seeded at beat 2600 by the round-4 kit (d3e2f4a1): latches 2064/2075/2079 pre-set AND UInt16[296] = 192, whose high byte zeroes hub byte 297

replay.expect: Every F0 run REPLAYS its stock PARTNER's walk before it tours: the partner's crossings that ENTERED another field -- landed, or reached the destination and were put back by it (the 353 bounce: "reached field N, but it never became playable", or, over inside the crossing's wait, the field the id first changed to) -- in order, in DONOR terms [place, exit index, entered place]; crossing attempts that never left the room are not part of the walk. Each step is crossed from the place the last one left him in, by the tour's own route_cross call under the tour's own failure()/strike rules -- a LIVE failure is retried in the same room while the run's budget holds, a REAL one strikes the step and BOUNCES (2) strikes break it; before the retry after a REAL failure he walks back to the spot the step's first attempt started from (a miss leaves him inside the zone, where a retry walks nowhere and fires nothing), by the same routing, a walk that strikes nothing -- and must ENTER the partner's place for that step; entering another place, standing anywhere but the step's place, or striking out stops the run "replay broke at step n (place.exit -> place): why" (VOID by coverage). The story moving on during the replay stops it there, as the tour stops ("SC left"), read right after each crossing and before it is judged: the crossing the story moved on at is never a divergence or a strike -- where the story's own move took him is the fork's doing. The whole walk replayed and SC still at the beat, the run goes on as the blind tour on the budget left, its stop reasons the tour's -- so an F0 whose story would move on later than its partner's still gets its chance. S and F4 runs are unchanged blind tours.
replay.partner: The round's F0 partners the round's S (the S run just before it in the frozen order). A re-run F0 partners a COVERED S run that has no covered F0 twin yet and whose walk has not broken max_breaks F0 replays already (F0 runs that partnered it and stopped "replay broke"), the oldest first; if there is none, S re-runs first for a fresh walk. Each covered S run is partnered by at most one covered F0 run. An F0 whose partner is VOID is VOID ("partner S#k VOID"), and so is one whose partner could not be read ("partner S#k unreadable"); the session records it without driving it. The session record (rung3_session.json) stores each F0 run's "partner" and the "walk" it was given; the analysis checks both, and recomputes every re-run's plan (which side, and whose walk) from the runs recorded before it, judged as the session judged them then (R3-RUNS: a re-run the plan did not name FAILs it), and reads the replay off the run's own log (coverage).
replay.log: every crossing the tour or a replay drives names the donor place it entered ("entered", or null), and carries route_cross's "changed_to" (the field the id first went to); a replay crossing is logged like a tour crossing with leg "replay", its "step" and the partner's place it "expect"s -- the walk back before a retry too, with "back" true and its "target" the spot. A log written before that is read the old way: landed, or the field route_cross's error names.

budget.why: step 1's stock run took ~11 min (segment ~2.5, tour 8.2); a tour gets 18 min (x2.2 stock's) on every side, the same rule everywhere; F4 never advances, so it runs to its passes or its 18 min. A run starts only with 12 min of the 3 h session left, and a tour never runs past the session's end. An F0 run's 18 min covers its replay and whatever tour follows it: the replay is its partner's own walk, ~8 min on session 2's pace. These numbers are v1's, unchanged, and so is expected_minutes, the plan they were sized on; session 2 MEASURED 559-787 s a run (9.3-13.1 min, mean 11.6) on every side -- F4 too: its tours ended on their 3 passes, never its 18 min -- and the nine in 6268 s (1 h 44 min), leaving the re-runs ("rerun") ~76 min.

coverage.expect: A run is COVERED -- evidence either way -- only when the drive gave it the chance to show what the checks read: its trace closed and it stood in its start field; the rows before that first row are New Game's and the harness's, read on neither side; its segment handed control back in 352 at the beat AFTER the wake (the log's segment record, and the wake's own store in the trace); its tour stopped the way its side's tour ends (clean_stop -- never STOPPED on an error, a donor mismatch, a broken replay, the session's budget, a skip, or the install changing under it); 351's lobby exit and 450's e19 exit both ran (their unconditional stores, member or seam alike); on S and F0 the controller flipped and the story reached SC 2610 (Garnet); on F4 a budget or passes stop came after at least as many crossings as the most any covered stock run needed to reach SC 2610. AND ON F0 (v2, "replay"): its partner is a covered stock run, and it replayed the partner's whole entered walk -- its log's replay steps, [place, exit, entered place] in order, ARE the partner's walk, every step entering the partner's place -- or, when the story moved on during the replay (the run stopped "SC left"), its steps BEFORE the crossing the story moved on at are the partner's first steps (the replay stops where the story moves, as the tour does; that crossing is never judged -- an early advance is the fork's, never the drive's). Every other run is VOID: listed with why, read by no check but R3-DONOR/R3-JOIN, and never a falsification. Each check reads only covered runs, and is VOID (not PASS) while a side it reads has fewer than min_covered.

rerun.why: after the nine, while a side has fewer than min_covered covered runs and a run still fits the session's budget, a run is added -- S first when S is short (every comparison and F4's crossing floor read it); then F0, partnering the oldest covered stock run with no covered F0 twin whose walk has not broken max_breaks replays, and when there is none S runs first for a fresh walk; then F4 -- at most max times. max is set from session 2's MEASURED pace, not v1's plan: runs of 559-787 s, mean 696 s, the nine in 6268 s. A run starts only while 720 s of the 10800 s are left, i.e. by 10080 s: at the mean, re-run k starts at 6268 + 696 (k - 1) s, and the 6th (9748 s) is the last that starts -- the 7th would need 10444; at 787 s a run, 5 start; a 7th fits only if the fifteen runs average under 672 s (11.2 min), below session 2's mean. So at measured pace the budget and max = 6 bind together, and it is the budget alone below that pace; the pairing can cost an extra run (a VOID stock run re-runs, then an F0 twins it; a walk that broke a replay costs a fresh S) and 6 leaves room for it. v1's cap was 4, its why v1's F4 estimate of ~22 min, which session 2 did not bear out. The cap stops a loop; the budget binds first everywhere else. The analysis reads EVERY run the session recorded -- a re-run adds a covered run, it never replaces or hides one.

P-FROZEN.expect: this file is byte-identical to the one the session recorded before its first run (the analysis reads the file the session names, unless told otherwise, and refuses a session whose F0 runs are not replays), and its member sets are the deployed chains' (rung3_forks.json)

R3-RUNS.expect: the session's runs are the frozen nine in order, then only re-runs (at most rerun.max); every recorded trace keeps the row contract, one traced run per file; the pairing is the registered one ("replay".partner): every F0 run names an earlier stock run as its partner, a round's F0 its round's S, the walk it was given is its partner's entered walk, no covered stock run is partnered by two covered F0 runs, and every re-run is the one the plan names (side, and whose walk) from the runs recorded before it; and each side has at least min_covered COVERED runs (short of that: VOID, listing why each run was)

R3-DONOR.expect: every row a fork run wrote in a member names that member's donor (ForkDonorPatch, live in the engine); every row in a real field names the field itself; no stock run stands in a fork id, no fork run in the other chain's ids -- over EVERY run read, covered or not

R3-JOIN.expect: 0 join failures and no note over every run read: every script row from the start field on joins a store in the bytes its side ran (a member's mod-folder .eb, the install's for a real field)

R3-PING.expect: the premise, stock: Bit[2102] := 1 written in every covered stock run, and WRITERS names only field 450 for it

R3-NULL-PRE.expect: F0, rung 2 at zone scale: no stock key written in every covered stock run before that run first stood in 450 is missing from every covered F0 run's MEMBER keys (a key F0 wrote only across the seam does not count as written); and it is not vacuous AT TOUR SCALE -- at least min_matched such keys are written by the members in every covered F0 run, and of those at least min_tour_keys were first written in every stock run during its TOUR (at or after its first row outside 352 after the wake), from at least the tour_donors. (v2) That non-vacuity guard read on the STOCK side alone -- fewer than min_matched stock keys before 450, fewer than min_tour_keys of them first written in every stock run's tour, or a tour_donor with none -- with nothing MISSING, is VOID with the shortfall named, not FAIL: the evidence the claim needs does not exist, which is coverage. The stock evidence there and the guard short only because the members wrote part of it in some covered F0 runs and not others (PARTIAL keys) is a FAIL, as in v1, naming them: a fork difference, not too little evidence. A MISSING key FAILs whatever the guard says.

R3-SEAM.expect: F0: in every covered run the first crossing out of the members is member(350) -> real 450, and every visit to 450 is across member(350)'s seam; 450's ping comes out as REACHED ONLY ACROSS A SEAM in every covered F0 run, under that crossing; no F0 member writes Bit[2102] := 1; and WRITERS names none of F0's donors for it (the report marks it: no member's donor writes it)

R3-MIRROR.expect: F0: FORK ONLY and STOCK ONLY are both empty and no neighbour-byte clobber -- a verbatim chain writes nothing its donors do not, and every stock key is matched by its members or reached across the seam

R3-ADVANCE.expect: F0's story moves on (its first row at SC >= 2610) in a REAL field, across the seam, in every covered run; no covered F4 run ever reaches SC 2610 (S's own advance is coverage, not a check)

R3-LATCH.expect: F4: (a) every hub-gated write below is STOCK ONLY at pattern level -- written in every covered stock run and by no covered F4 run (members or across the seam) outside the seed's own prepend; (b) the CLOBBER report names byte 297 changed 1 -> 0 by the prepend's UInt16[296] = 192, in every covered F4 run, on stock evidence that byte 297 is UInt16[297]'s; (c) not vacuous: every covered F4 run entered the real 450 across member(350)'s seam (and, by coverage, walked out through e19 and took 351's lobby exit), so the 450 and 351 writes are absent where their gateways ran

the controller's flip, any room: Bit[2075] := 1

R3-PREEMPT.expect: F4, the latches' own half (round 5's fix, named by the trace): PRE-EMPTED names each round-4 latch -- the prepend stamps it in every covered F4 run (FORK ONLY, off < 0) and every covered stock run writes it itself at the site below: 2064 at 351's lobby exit, 2079/2075 at the controller's flip, in whichever room

NC-THROW.expect: nothing thrown through the event engine, the evaluator, the tracer or the agent

not_failed: UNSTABLE keys are listed, not failed. F4's absent ping has two causes the trace cannot separate (297 = 0 fails 450 e19's hub term, 2079 = 1 its latch term): R3-LATCH names the clobber's evidence and R3-PREEMPT the latches', and neither claims which gate stopped the ping. Separating them needs a chain with the latches but 297 intact (F4b: the words written as bytes) -- not in this session: 11 more ids, and ~66 min more than the 3 h cap holds.
